title: CHORD: Composable Hybrid Optical Reconfigurable Diffractive Framework For Optical Neural Network
problem: Diffractive optical neural networks (DONNs) offer ultra-parallel, high-efficiency computing via freespace light propagation, but lack reconfigurability due to fixed post-fabrication optical structures, limiting practical deployment for dynamic AI workloads.
motivation: DONNs promise exceptional speed and energy efficiency for AI, but static hardware cannot adapt to evolving applications and workloads.
method: CHORD combines fixed optical hardware (built into the chip and unchangeable) with adjustable electronic controls. During training, the system learns the best control settings for each task, optimizing them across the entire system. This allows one physical chip to handle many different AI problems. It pairs the speed advantage of optical computing — which uses light to naturally parallelize operations — with the flexibility of electronically adjustable settings.
key_novelty: By combining fixed optical hardware with learnable electronic controls, CHORD enables exponentially more different AI tasks.
contributions: Full-system learnability enabling repurposing of fixed optical hardware
Exponentially larger functional space compared to prior DONNs
74x faster speed and 194x lower energy than digital with digital-comparable accuracy
primary_theme: Hybrid optical/photonic reconfigurable DONN with learnable system variables
